title: Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang; Dow Soars 1,500 Points, Nasdaq Up 6.7%, S&P 500 Rises – Live Updates
body:
Wall Street surged on Monday as the Dow Jones Industrial Average leapt more than 1,500 points, the Nasdaq Composite rallied 6.7 percent, and the S&P 500 vaulted to fresh highs. The rally was sparked by the unexpected decision of Nvidia’s board to reinstate founder‑CEO Jensen Huang after a brief, tumultuous period of leadership uncertainty, a move that sent Nvidia stock soaring roughly 30 percent and ignited a broader technology‑driven bounce across equity markets.

Investors greeted Huang’s return as a vote of confidence in the company’s strategic direction, especially as Nvidia continues to dominate the artificial‑intelligence chip market. The chipmaker’s valuation, already perched near $1 trillion, surged past the $1.2 trillion mark in a single session, wiping out weeks of profit‑taking and restoring optimism that the AI boom will sustain high growth rates. Analysts at major banks upgraded Nvidia to “outperform,” citing the firm’s expanding data‑center orders, its recent partnership announcements with leading cloud providers, and the expectation that its next‑generation H100 GPUs will cement its lead over rivals such as AMD and Intel.

The ripple effect of the Nvidia news was evident in the broader market. The technology‑heavy Nasdaq, which had been lagging behind the Dow and S&P 500 in recent weeks, posted its strongest daily gain in over a year, driven by sizable jumps in other AI‑related stocks, including Microsoft, Alphabet, and Amazon, all of which reported better‑than‑expected earnings earlier in the week. The Dow’s surge was anchored by traditional industrials and financials that benefited from the overall risk‑on sentiment, while the S&P 500’s climb reflected a balanced lift across sectors, suggesting that investors are now viewing the AI narrative as a catalyst for earnings growth beyond pure tech names.

Market psychologists note that the speed and magnitude of the rally underscore how closely investors have tied the health of the broader equity market to the fortunes of a single company. “Nvidia has become the poster child for AI, and its fortunes are now a proxy for the sector’s trajectory,” said Laura Cheng, senior market strategist at Meridian Capital. “When the board signaled stability by bringing back Huang, it removed a major source of uncertainty and allowed investors to refocus on fundamentals.” However, Cheng cautioned that such concentration also raises volatility risks, especially if future earnings guidance falls short of the lofty expectations set by the current hype.

The reinstatement also resolves a governance dispute that had lingered since a surprise boardroom shake‑up in early March, when a faction of directors attempted to replace Huang amid concerns about over‑expansion and supply‑chain constraints. The board’s reversal, after a closed‑door session with Huang and senior executives, was framed as a “unified commitment to long‑term value creation.” Corporate governance experts view the episode as a reminder that even high‑growth tech firms must balance visionary leadership with board oversight, especially as they navigate regulatory scrutiny and geopolitical tensions that could affect semiconductor supply chains.

Looking ahead, the market’s next test will be whether the AI‑driven optimism can translate into sustained earnings growth across the broader economy. Upcoming earnings reports from major cloud providers and chip manufacturers will be closely watched for signs of demand elasticity, while the Federal Reserve’s policy stance remains a wildcard amid lingering inflation concerns. For now, the extraordinary rally has restored confidence in a market that had been wobbling on the edge of a correction, and investors will be keen to see if the momentum can be maintained without a sharp pullback once the initial euphoria settles.

If the AI sector continues to deliver robust revenue expansion and Nvidia can keep its technological edge, the current surge could mark the beginning of a new era of market growth. Conversely, any misstep—whether a supply bottleneck, regulatory hurdle, or a missed earnings target—could quickly erode the gains and reignite volatility. In the coming weeks, traders and analysts alike will be watching the interplay between corporate performance, policy decisions, and global supply dynamics to gauge whether today’s rally is a fleeting spike or the foundation of a longer‑term upward trajectory.
